extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants / PIs and senior/key personnel preparing PHS 398 (NIH) grant applications and resubmissions
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and revising an NIH PHS 398 research grant application (resubmission), including biosketches, research plan, budget justification, and responses to reviewer critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — overall format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, eRA Commons user name (credential), position title, education/training table, and the required labeled sections (A. Personal statement; B. Positions and honors; C. Contributions to science). Use the provided format for each person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training table requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date (MM/YYYY), and field of study. Begin with undergraduate and include subsequent training (postdoc/residency) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Personal statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize your specific contributions and relevance to the proposed project, describe the role you will play (e.g., which aims you will lead), highlight key publications and ongoing collaborations that support your qualifications. Use this to justify fit to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — Positions and honors
rubrics_metrics.description: B. Positions and honors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological list of positions/employment and honors relevant to the investigator, including dates. This demonstrates track record and suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — Contributions to science
rubrics_metrics.description: C. Contributions to science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbered narrative vignettes describing major contributions, the historical context, significance, and key representative citations. Each contribution should include brief supporting references (a., b., c., ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research support — ongoing and completed
rubrics_metrics.description: List Ongoing Research Support and Completed Research Support with project title, role (PI/Co-PI), major goal, and dates (e.g., 8/1/03 – 7/31/17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevance of each support item for the current application (role and how the project relates). For completed support, include role and project summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Human Subjects Section — Clinical Trial? (Yes/No) and Agency-Defined Phase III Clinical Trial? (Yes/No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare whether the proposed project involves clinical trials; if yes, identify the phase and follow any additional required documentation and plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: 2. Vertebrate Animals Section — Are vertebrate animals euthanized? If 'Yes' to euthanasia: Is the method consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) guidelines? If 'No' to AVMA guidelines, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state euthanasia plans and compliance with AVMA; if deviating, provide justification. This section must be answered and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Program Income
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. Program Income Section — Is program income anticipated during the periods for which the grant support is requested? (Yes/No). If 'Yes', use the format to reflect amount and source(s) by Budget Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If anticipating program income, list anticipated amounts, sources, and budget periods in the specified format; if no program income, leave blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESC)
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. Human Embryonic Stem Cells Section — Does the proposed project involve human embryonic stem cells? (Yes/No). If 'Yes', list registration number(s) from the NIH registry or check the box that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hESCs are involved, provide registry numbers or indicate that a registry line will be used; otherwise indicate 'No'.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Inventions and Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. Inventions and Patents Section (RENEWAL) — Inventions and Patents: (Yes/No). If 'Yes', indicate Previously Reported (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare whether inventions/patents exist and, if renewal, whether previously reported; provide further details if required by the application type.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Change of Investigator/Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: 6. Change of Investigator / Change of Institution Section — Name of former Project Director / Principal Investigator, Change of Project Director / Principal Investigator fields, Change of Grantee Institution fields, and related identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete this section when applicable, including names and prior/new institution details to document administrative changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan — required section list
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Research Plan — required components: Introduction (resubmission/revision), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Data Safety Monitoring Plan, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the Research Plan using these labeled sections. Include the appropriate document names (e.g., Introduction-resubmission.pdf, Specific_Aims-resubmission.pdf, Research_Strategy-Final_resubmission.pdf) and supporting files (vertebrate_animals_Novick.pdf, letters_of_support.pdf, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel: list personnel, percent effort or months (e.g., Tom W. Muir (1 summer month), Postdoc: 12 months), describe responsibilities (experimental design, interpretation, specific aims), and provide salary & fringe/benefits justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the role of each person, effort requested (months or percent), and rationale tying responsibilities to aims. Include benefits and salary calculations for each personnel line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — materials & supplies (itemized categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials & Supplies: justify categories and quantities (e.g., HPLC/FPLC columns — analytical and semi-prep counts and sizes; solvents volumes per synthesis; Boc-L-amino acids calculations; SPPS chemicals; cloning reagents; microbiological media; chromatography media; proteases; electrophoresis supplies; sequencing and oligo synthesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed, itemized justification for consumables based on anticipated experimental throughput (e.g., number of peptide syntheses per year, solvent liters per synthesis) and based on actual lab records or standard practice. Include unit costs where possible and total costs per category and year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — travel and publication costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel: request per year for travel to domestic scientific meetings and synchrotron trips; specify number of trips per person (1 per postdoc/grad student and PI). Publication Costs: request an annual amount to meet publication and reprint costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the number and purpose of trips, estimate per-trip costs, and provide a yearly total. Provide a yearly figure for publication fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification — animals and supplies per researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals: funds requested for purchase and maintenance of mice required for proposed experiments (yearly request). Supplies: funds requested at a stated per-year per-researcher rate (e.g., usual rate for workers in Novick lab). Miscellaneous: funds requested for travel to one domestic meeting per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-animal and per-researcher cost estimates and justify based on experimental needs and institutional norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget line-item calculation transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When specific calculations are given (e.g., peptide synthesis: ~10 syntheses per year; 2.20 mmol amino acid per residue; average formula weight 280 g/mole; solvents per synthesis volumes), include the arithmetic and assumptions used to arrive at quantities and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document calculation methods and assumptions so reviewers can verify that requested amounts are reasonable and grounded in standard lab practices or prior records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission introduction — addressing reviewer critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to Application (Resubmission and Revision): explicitly acknowledge prior review, summarize reviewers' overall evaluation, and state how the major weaknesses/criticisms were addressed in the revision (e.g., reorganize Aim 3, replace mouse experiments with new sub-aim, add preliminary data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a point-by-point discussion of critiques and responses, include new preliminary data/figures, justify methodological choices, explain feasibility, and describe alternative approaches (candidate and unbiased). Show how revisions respond to reviewers' concerns and strengthen the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to technical feasibility critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers question feasibility of ambitious experiments, provide newly added preliminary data, methodological details (e.g., x-ray crystal structure at 2.25 Å, photocrosslinking localization to residues 75–90), and outline complementary approaches (mapping, targeted mutagenesis, genetic incorporation of crosslinkers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate feasibility with concrete data, describe fallback or parallel strategies (both candidate and unbiased approaches), and provide experimental milestones or evidence that supports the planned work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document naming and attachments convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific file naming for submission components (e.g., Introduction-resubmission.pdf, Specific_Aims-resubmission.pdf, Research_Strategy-Final_resubmission.pdf, Vertebrate_animals_Novick.pdf, Letters_of_Support.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize upload package using clear filenames matching the Research Plan sections to ensure reviewers can find revised materials and supporting documents.
